reference.source: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry / Braunwald's Heart Disease
clinicalPearls: ApoB-48 is produced by enterocyte RNA editing of ApoB mRNA; full-length ApoB-100 is produced in liver and present on VLDL, IDL and LDL
ApoC-II activates endothelial lipoprotein lipase (LPL); ApoE mediates hepatic clearance of remnants and chylomicrons
Type I hyperchylomicronemia: LPL or ApoC-II deficiency; massive fasting chylomicrons, creamy layer, eruptive xanthomas, acute pancreatitis
Type IIa familial hypercholesterolemia: autosomal dominant LDL receptor mutations; elevated LDL, tendon xanthomas, premature CAD in 30s-40s
HDL mediates reverse cholesterol transport; ApoA-I activates LCAT; CETP transfers cholesterol esters from HDL to VLDL in exchange for triglycerides
reference.pathophysiology: Familial hypercholesterolemia results in defective clearance of circulating LDL particles, leading to accelerated atherogenesis, subendothelial foam cell accumulation and fibrous plaque formation. Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia (Type III) results from homozygosity for ApoE2, which binds poorly to hepatic receptors, causing accumulation of chylomicron remnants and IDL with palmar xanthomas.
additionalInvestigations: Fasting lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides)
Genetic testing for LDLR, APOB, and PCSK9 pathogenic variants
